problem: Brokers and carriers burn staff time on manual order entry, quoting, load building and appointment scheduling from emails and documents.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage priced AI agents (pricing not verified)

founders.name: Mike Carter
prior_employers: Kodiak Robotics (founding engineer, led motion planning and safety)
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on YC page.

founders.name: Jesse Buckingham
prior_employers: ASG LogisTech (CEO, grew from about $2M to over $20M ARR per YC page)
education: Stanford Graduate School of Business, MBA (per YC page)

investors: Angels from Motive, project44, Ryder, Uber

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting orders from emails and documents and integrating with TMS systems was feasible with 2023 language models; the hard part was integrations and accuracy.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with TMS, rating and carrier systems add stickiness, but many YC and other startups target freight brokerage automation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Turvo announced a partnership with Vooma rather than copying it; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Freight brokers handled heavy manual email order entry; Vooma reports 12.5x revenue growth in the year before December 2024 (company reported).

branding.domain_note: Moved from vooma.ai to vooma.com (301 redirect observed 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, energetic, benefit focused; speaks to overworked staff.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Vooma paired a self driving truck engineer with a logistics software CEO and sold AI order entry to brokers, reaching 40 people and customers such as Echo, NFI and ArcBest. It raised $16.6M across seed and Series A in December 2024 and no later round was found.
notes: Seed date is the announcement date, actual close unknown. Aggregators show $14M or $14.2M variants; press release figures used. No competitor list dated near the batch was found; searches returned only 2025 to 2026 vendor comparison pages, which are not valid as of founding. FleetWorks (YC S23) and MVMNT appeared as contemporaries but no source dates their state at Vooma's founding. Name origin not found.
